chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the woman who disavows her husband or divorces him by Khul'a, with two witnesses, upon a period of purity without sexual intercourse, asking if she would be irrevocably divorced from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is as you have mentioned, then yes.' I said: 'It has been reported to us that she is not irrevocably divorced from him until the divorce follows it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So that is not Khul'a.' I said: 'She is irrevocably divorced from him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.تَخْتَلِعُ: To divorce by Khul'a, where the wife pays compensation
key_terms.تُبَارِئُ: Disavowment (Mubarat), a type of divorce initiated by the wife
key_terms.خُلْعًا: Khul'a, a specific form of divorce

ai.seo_question: Does a Khul'a divorce with witnesses result in immediate irrevocable divorce?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that a Mubarat divorce initiated by the wife with two witnesses during a period of purity (without sexual intercourse) results in an immediate, irrevocable separation (Bain), distinguishing it from standard Khul'a which typically requires a subsequent divorce pronouncement. This ruling addresses the scholarly debate on whether the mutual agreement itself constitutes the final dissolution or merely the first stage, affirming the immediacy of the bond's severance in this specific context. The emphasis on 'two witnesses' and 'purity' underscores the procedural rigor required to prevent ambiguity in marital status within Shia jurisprudence.
